To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
knockdown of YY1a can lead to downregulate the expression of PSR in zebrafish, which may cause the abnormal development of brain and heart.
YY1a plays a role in the development of the brain and heart through regulation of the PSR-mediated engulfing apoptotic cells.

YY1a knock-down by morpholino oligos leads to down-regulation of the zebrafish PSR receptor during embryonic segmentation, which in turn leads to the accumulation of large numbers of dead apoptotic cell in the posterior part of the developing embryo and the interference with embryonic cell-cell interactions that are essential for normal development of the brain, heart and eyes.

the role of YY1a in the PSR-mediated engulfment of dead cells in the developing embryo.
the role of YY1a in the regulation of apoptotic cell engulfing system during zebrafish development and its possible implication in diseases.
the role of YY1a in the regulation of apoptotic cell death in developing zebfish.

the PSR-mediated engulfing process is essential for embryonic development and YY1a is an important regulator in the apoptotic process.
YY1a/ PSR-mediated engulfing is a fundamental mechanism for normal development and YY1a/ zebrafish PSR may be a potential target for future drug design.
the YY1a/ PSR-mediated engulfing pathway is involved in zebrafish brain and heart development and may be a target for the development of new therapeutic approaches.
